title: Reliability Compass: Initiative gating, forecasted error‑budget runway, and automation hooks
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Teams lack a lightweight, automated way to gate initiatives against projected error‑budget runway and to surface corrective actions early. Current manual spreadsheets and ad‑hoc Slack alerts create inconsistent decisions and late rollbacks.

Objective: Build a product‑level "Reliability Compass" feature in the Console that: (1) ingests SLI burn rate and historical SLO attainment, (2) projects error‑budget runway per service and initiative, (3) exposes gating signals for rollouts (green/yellow/red) with reasons, and (4) provides automation hooks (webhooks/runbook links/CI gates) to throttle or pause rollouts when thresholds are crossed.

Deliverables:
- Console data model and UI for per‑initiative runway forecast and gating state.
- Backend pipeline to compute short‑term runway (1, 7, 30 days) using burn‑rate models and Monte Carlo scenario for high variance SLIs.
- Gate API that emits events and supports rule templates (e.g., pause if 7d runway < 3 days and burn acceleration > 1.5x).
- Integration recipes for CI/CD (GitHub Actions), rollout controller, and incident runbook links.

Scope notes: We target hosted and Dedicated customers first. Private/VPC integration will follow (config mapping only). This ticket covers design, backend prototype, and Console UI MVP for a single SLI group (inference latency p95) and generic rollout gating rules.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows runway projection card for at least one SLI group with 1d/7d/30d estimates
Backend job produces runway projections within 5% of Monte Carlo baseline for synthetic test harness
Gate API emits events when a rule template is violated and includes metadata (service, initiative, current burn, projection)
Two automation recipes documented: GitHub Actions gate and Rollout controller webhook, each with example payloads
Onboarded pilot with SRE+Payments team on Dedicated cluster for 2‑week trial and documented feedback
comments: 2025-01-12 — Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes. Agreed scope: p95 latency SLI, one initiative view, basic Monte Carlo model. Action: Jonah to draft data schema and required telemetry. Links to PRD in Confluence added.

2025-01-20 — Jonah Park: Data schema v0 posted. Need to ingest per‑route token counts and per‑request latency histogram buckets. Blocker: unified telemetry missing for some Dedicated customers. Filed ENG dependency ENG-41234.

2025-01-28 — Priya Desai (SRE): Reviewed projection model. Suggested adding a short‑term exponential smoothing baseline to complement Monte Carlo for bursty workloads. Jonah to prototype both and compare on historical 2024 incidents dataset.

2025-02-03 — Design review (Liam O'Connor): Console card wireframes look good; recommended emphasizing 'recommended action' button and quick link to rollback/pausing playbooks. Added a11y checklist item.

2025-02-10 — Jonah Park: Backend prototype completed for Monte Carlo and smoothing hybrid. Initial smoke tests on staging show runway estimate stable on non‑burst periods; further tuning required for daily spikes. Preparing demo for Payments SRE on 2025-02-14.
2025-02-12 — Ava Martinez: Updated acceptance criteria to include automation recipes. Confirmed pilot start date 2025-02-17 with Payments team.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP) — 1 service, hosted + Dedicated staging: projection card + gate API + GitHub Action recipe
Phase 2 — Pilot with Payments SRE on Dedicated production; iterate rules and smoothing parameters
Phase 3 — Expand to additional SLIs and add policy editor in Console; Private/VPC integration mapping
Phase 4 — Expose templated recovery playbooks and automated partial throttles via rollout controller
notes: Tradeoffs: Monte Carlo provides robust tails but is compute‑heavy; hybrid approach chosen to balance accuracy and cost.
Decision: Gate severity will be three states (ok/warning/critical) with human confirmation required for 'critical' automated pauses in production for Dedicated customers.
Open question: Should we include cost impact estimate alongside runway? MVP will surface only SLI runway; follow‑up ticket to model dollars saved by throttling.
